validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/OWNERSHIP (high, 2 independent origins): confirmed by TWO separately-published corporate press releases describing the same transaction from opposite sides of the deal — (1) Cardinal Midstream Partners' own Feb 6 2023 release, distributed via Business Wire (wayback: businesswire.com/.../Cardinal-Midstream-Closes-on-Acquisition-of-Medallion... , captured 2023-03-14, 'Cardinal Midstream Partners...has closed its previously announced acquisition of Medallion Midstream Services' natural gas gathering and processing business in the prolific Delaware Basin in West Texas. The newly acquired business spans Reeves and Loving counties and includes approximately 80 miles of high- and low-pressure natural gas gathering pipelines...'), and (2) Medallion Midstream's OWN separate release on its own site (wayback: medallionmidstream.com/news/medallion-closes-sale-natural-gas-business, captured 2023-12-06, quoting Medallion CEO Randy Lentz confirming the same sale of 'its natural gas gathering and processing business in the Delaware Basin to Cardinal Midstream Partners'). These are genuinely independent (buyer vs. seller, two different companies/domains), not one wire story reprinted — both corroborate the pipeline's existence, Delaware Basin location, gathering classification, and Cardinal Midstream as 100% owner. A third outlet, Pipeline & Gas Journal (pgjonline.com, live and verifier-clean), reports the identical facts (80 miles, Reeves/Loving counties, Cardinal buyer) but is a trade-press paraphrase of the SAME Cardinal press release — per the independence rule this is the SAME origin as the Business Wire release, not a third one, so I am not double-counting it. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=gathering is CORRECT and explicitly confirmed — both releases call it a 'natural gas gathering and processing business' / 'gathering pipelines', not a transmission trunk. No FERC docket exists for this line (expected — gathering systems are not FERC-jurisdictional), so FERC silence is not an existence concern here. DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against the full 45-row Texas roster — no other row describes a Reeves/Loving County Cardinal Midstream gathering system; this is not a relabel of any other listed pipeline. LOCATION: gem.wiki's own infobox (read for leads only, never cited) adds 'The pipeline runs around Orla, Texas' — Orla sits in Reeves County, consistent with both press releases and with GEM's existing Texas/Texas Start/EndState. I did not force StartLocation/EndLocation to Reeves vs. Loving specifically: this is a GATHERING system (multiple wellpad connections into a processing hub), not a linear point-to-point line, so assigning one county as 'start' and the other as 'end' would be an invented directionality neither source states — left blank rather than fabricated, per the fills guidance. LENGTH (medium, single origin): the 80-mile figure traces to exactly one origin — Cardinal's own Feb 2023 release — repeated verbatim by PGJ; Medallion's independent release does not restate a mileage figure, so I cannot upgrade Length past medium despite two press outlets carrying it. CAPACITY/DIAMETER: both sources cite a '140 MMcf/d' figure, but that number belongs to the co-acquired NATURAL GAS PROCESSING FACILITY, a separate asset from the gathering pipeline itself — applying it to this pipeline row's Capacity field would be a misattribution, so I deliberately left Capacity and Diameter blank/unfilled rather than force a wrong number onto the wrong asset. STATUS=operating: inferred by context, not literal — the transaction closed Feb 2023 transferring an active, in-service gathering system; no source indicates idling or decommissioning. Harvested-pool coverage: all 4 of this row's harvested wiki citations were opened and screened (2 medallionmidstream.com URLs 404 live but recovered via Wayback; 1 businesswire.com URL times out intermittently on direct fetch but resolves via its Wayback snapshot and passed url_verifier repeatedly; 1 pgjonline.com URL is live and verifier-clean directly) — nothing in the pool was left unopened.
